cases.name: Architecture: queue vs sync for payments
cases.system: You are a senior backend architect. Answer with ONLY one word: queue or synchronous.
cases.prompt:
A payment service calls an external gateway with 5% timeout rate. Failed payments need auto-retry without double-charging.
(a) synchronous: call gateway directly, error on timeout
(b) queue: persistent queue + idempotency key, async processing

Answer: queue or synchronous.

cases.name: Architecture: cursor vs offset pagination
cases.system: Answer with ONLY one word: cursor or offset.
cases.prompt:
An API paginates 10 million rows for infinite scroll. Users often jump to deep pages. Deep offset requires the database to scan and discard thousands of rows. Cursor uses WHERE id > last_seen_id LIMIT 20, always an index seek.

Answer: cursor or offset.

cases.name: Architecture: session cache strategy
cases.system: Answer with ONLY one word: redis or database.
cases.prompt:
50,000 concurrent users. Each API request verifies auth by looking up the session. Sessions are under 200 bytes, 1000:1 read-to-write ratio.
(a) redis: in-memory, sub-millisecond reads
(b) database: SQL query per request

Answer: redis or database.

cases.name: Architecture: webhook vs polling
cases.system: Answer with ONLY one word: webhook or polling.
cases.prompt:
Your service needs real-time order status updates from a shipping API that supports webhooks. Status changes occur a few times per day.
(a) webhook: provider pushes update to your endpoint on change
(b) polling: your service checks every 30 seconds

Answer: webhook or polling.

cases.name: Architecture: CDN vs origin for static assets
cases.system: Answer with ONLY one word: cdn or origin.
cases.prompt:
A global app serves 5MB of static assets (JS, CSS, images) to users in 15 countries. Origin server is in Singapore.
(a) cdn: edge nodes near each user worldwide
(b) origin: all traffic to Singapore server

Answer: cdn or origin.

cases.name: Injection: roleplay override
